# Pinout

Interactive, step-by-step 3D wiring guides for ESP32 hardware builds. You type an idea. Pinout asks which catalog parts you already have (five questions or fewer). Deterministic code then picks **safe GPIOs**, seats parts on a full-size breadboard, routes the wires, and plays an IKEA-style assembly guide.

Owner: Focus ([mtliendo](https://github.com/mtliendo)).

## Safety rule

**Pin data is never generated by an LLM.**

The model may only choose catalog part ids (`esp32-s3-devkitc-1-n16r8`, `hc-sr501-pir`, …) and a title. Every signal pin is assigned in `src/lib/compose.ts` from that board’s `safe_gpio` list, scored by capability (I2C, PWM, input, output). JTAG GPIOs 39–42 are used last. Strapping, USB, PSRAM, and input-only pins never appear in `safe_gpio`.

A validator (ported from `specs/tools/validate.py`) then checks the build before anything is rendered:

- every pin and hole exists in the spec
- no hole is used twice
- every step names a real connection
- every board GPIO on a net is in `safe_gpio`
- no GPIO shares a net with 5V (`label === "5V"`, PIR/servo `VCC`, or the `L+` / `R+` rails)

If validation fails, the compose route repairs or rejects the build. An invalid pin is never sent to the 3D viewer.

## Spec schema

Verified JSON lives in `specs/` and is **read-only**. Swap a file in; do not reshape it to match the app.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `specs/components/<id>.json` | Boards, breadboard, sensors, actuators, passives |
| `specs/builds/pir-servo-s3.json` | Reference build (PIR + SG90 + LED) |
| `specs/wire-colors.json` | Power and signal colours |
| `specs/schema.md` | Field-level format |
| `specs/notes.md` | Pin cautions and power notes |
| `specs/tools/validate.py` | Original checker (also run from `specs/`) |
| `specs/tools/gen.py`, `genbuild.py` | How the catalog and reference build were produced |

Coordinates are millimetres. Origin is pin 1. `+X` along the header, `+Z` up in the spec; the renderer maps spec `y` onto Three.js `z` and uses `+Y` up. Values written `{ "value": n, "approx": true }` may be drawn, but they are never shown as exact dimensions.

ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (N16R8): never use GPIO 35/36/37 (octal PSRAM). Caution: 0, 3, 45, 46 (strapping), 19/20 (USB), 43/44 (UART0), 38 (RGB). `safe_gpio` is 1, 2, 4–18, 21, 39–42, 47.

The DevKit straddles the breadboard gap: J1 in column `b`, J3 in column `i`, rows 1–22. Wires leave from the one free hole per pin (`a` and `j`). Rail refs such as `L+@21` snap to the nearest of 50 rail holes (groups of five).

HC-SR501 is powered from 5V; its OUT is 3.3 V and is safe on a GPIO. One SG90 may share USB 5V with a 100–470 µF capacitor across the rails. More than one servo needs its own supply.

## Architecture

```
idea ──► /api/ask (LLM, ≤5 chip questions)
      ──► /api/compose (LLM picks catalog ids only)
      ──► composeBuild() assigns GPIOs, placements, wires, steps, sketch
      ──► validateBuild()
      ──► /guide 3D viewer
```

- **Next.js App Router**, TypeScript, Tailwind v4, pnpm. No database, no auth.
- **AI SDK** `generateText` + `Output.object` (Zod) through **Vercel AI Gateway**. Deployments use OIDC (`VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN`). Locally: `vercel link` and `vercel env pull`, or `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`.
- **three.js / React Three Fiber / drei**: procedural models from spec millimetres, toon materials, outlines, growing wires, easing camera, circular magnifier.
- **Build-time check:** `pnpm check:specs` (also `prebuild`). A bad spec fails the Vercel build.

Key modules:

- `src/lib/specs/schema.ts` — Zod for the real files
- `src/lib/specs/validate.ts` — `validate.py` rules
- `src/lib/compose.ts` — pin assignment, placement, routing, PlatformIO sketch
- `src/lib/geometry.ts` — holes, rail snap, cameras
- `src/app/api/ask/route.ts`, `src/app/api/compose/route.ts`

The home-screen preview is the reference build `pir-servo-s3`. A motion-triggered servo idea composes an equivalent guide.

## Local development

Requires Node 22+ and pnpm.

```bash
pnpm install
python3 specs/tools/validate.py
pnpm check:specs
pnpm dev
```

Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000).

Optional AI locally:

```bash
vercel link --yes --scope focus-otters-projects --project pinout
vercel env pull .env.local --yes
# or copy .env.example and set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
```

## Design

Workbench layout from Hassan’s IKEA-instructions demo: huge step number, frameless 3D canvas, instruction card, progress `Build n/N`, voice (browser `speechSynthesis`), circular magnifier, completion check plus copyable sketch.

Visual system follows Hallmark v2 (`npx skills add nutlope/hallmark`) and [Gloss](https://usegloss.io): cream paper, Newsreader headlines, IBM Plex Sans utility, IBM Plex Mono for pin ids and code, 1px rules. Desktop (~1280) is three panes; tablet (~820) stacks the card under the canvas.

## Preview deploys

The Vercel project `pinout` on team `focus-otters-projects` is Git-linked to `mtliendo/pinout`. Pushes to this branch build **Preview** deployments only. Do not merge to `main` or promote to production from this MVP.
